lesson_title: Three Territories, One Map: Paper 1 Physics Essentials
hook_text: At the top of the throw the ball 'stops'... and thousands of learners hand back a mark. Gravity never clocked out.
clip_script: The acceleration is 9,8 metres per second squared downward at every instant — at the top of the flight the velocity is zero but the acceleration is still 9,8, and that exact statement appears in the paper year after year. The traps in Paper 1 are old friends wearing new numbers, so meet them by name. Trap one: the top of the flight. Velocity is zero there, and the trap whispers that acceleration is too — it is not; gravity works full shifts, 9,8 metres per second squared, all the way up and all the way down.
visual_style: A ball arcing up in slow motion, freezing at the apex with a giant zero over its velocity vector while the g arrow keeps pulsing downward; a memo tick landing on the correct statement.
mood: Myth-busting energy — catching the whisper of the trap in the act.
pacing: Slow-motion rise to the freeze-frame, beat of silence at the apex, rapid-fire correction and payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full Paper 1 revision sweep and disarm all four classic traps.
